item.title: [Exclusive] Election Commissioners Skip Work on Election Day ([단독] 선거날도 출근 안 한다, 유명무실 선관위원)
item.description:
[Exclusive] Election Commissioners Skip Work on Election Day ([단독] 선거날도 출근 안 한다, 유명무실 선관위원)

On the day of the June 3 local elections, only two members showed up at the central office of the National Election Commission (NEC) in Gwacheon, Gyeonggi Province: then-NEC Chairperson Noh Tae-ak (who later resigned), a non-standing member, and standing commissioner Wi Cheol-hwan (currently acting NEC Chairperson). According to data submitted by the NEC on the 14th to the office of People Power Party lawmaker Kim Eun-hye, the seven non-standing commissioners did not attend. <<> Criticism has been raised that non-standing members should at least be present at the office on election day, but an NEC official stated, “Non-standing commissioners only attend meetings when convened to vote on agendas; they typically do not come in on local election days.” This is reportedly how the NEC’s operational system works. At the Seoul Metropolitan Election Commission, only five out of eight commissioners—including the chairperson and standing members—showed up at the office or the vote-counting situation room on the 3rd. <<> However, on the afternoon of the 3rd, a voting suspension incident occurred in Songpa-gu, Seoul, due to a shortage of ballots. An emergency meeting of the NEC was only convened at midnight on the 4th. According to a comprehensive investigation by this newspaper, the meeting was initially not planned, but was arranged after the People Power Party made a protest visit. Some polling stations in Songpa-gu, where voting hours had been extended until 10 PM, saw the unprecedented situation of voters casting ballots while watching exit polls and vote-counting broadcasts from news outlets. <<> The NEC, established in 1963—three years after the April 19 Revolution—was granted constitutional status as an independent body to prevent “government-rigged elections.” The system has operated for over 60 years with a dual structure: commissioners composed mainly of legal professionals and scholars, and a secretariat handling practical affairs. Analysts say this incident has exposed a structural problem in the NEC where no one takes responsibility. <<> Such issues were already evident during the so-called “basket voting” incident of the early voting period for the March 5, 2022, presidential election. Even then-NEC Chairperson Noh Jeong-hee did not come to the office that day, and the NEC responded at the time, “It follows precedent as a non-standing member.” The emergency committee meeting was held only two days later, on the 7th. Experts warn, “If the central election commissioners are not made full-time and control over election bureaucrats is not strengthened, this will keep repeating.” <<> Meanwhile, President Lee Jae-myung, who was on a visit to Italy, chaired a video conference with senior advisors on the 14th, stating, “We fully acknowledge and accept the public’s legitimate questions about the infringement of voting rights,” but added, “There are factions exploiting this to incite absurd conspiracy theories.” He also described the spread of election fraud claims as “distorting the essence of the issue” and an “anti-social behavior.” (6·3 지방선거 당일, 경기 과천시 중앙선관위 사무실에 나온 중앙선관위원은 비상임인 노태악 당시 중앙선관위원장(사퇴)과 위철환 상임위원(현 중앙선관위원장 직무대행) 등 2명이었다. 14일 중앙선관위가 국민의힘 김은혜 의원실에 제출한 자료에 따르면 비상임위원 7명은 나오지 않았다.)

item.title: Aiming at the Activist Generation That Used to Preach Democracy: The Ballot Paper Disaster and the Fury of the 2030 Generation (민주주의 훈계하던 운동권 세대를 조준하다… 투표용지 참사와 2030의 분노)
item.description:
Aiming at the Activist Generation That Used to Preach Democracy: The Ballot Paper Disaster and the Fury of the 2030 Generation (민주주의 훈계하던 운동권 세대를 조준하다… 투표용지 참사와 2030의 분노)

This local election has left a stain on history as the most poorly managed election in constitutional history. This catastrophe, dubbed the "ballot paper shortage crisis," goes beyond mere administrative errors at some polling stations; it has stripped voters of their most sacred right—the right to vote—and shattered trust in the nation's electoral management capabilities. (이번 지방선거는 헌정 사상 유례없는 부실 선거 관리로 기억될 오점을 남겼다. 이른바 ‘투표용지 부족 사태’로 명명된 이번 참사는 단순히 일부 투표소 행정적 실수를 넘어, 유권자의 가장 신성한 권리인 참정권을 박탈하고 국가 선거 관리 역량에 대한 신뢰를 무너뜨렸다.)

Initially dismissed as an unexpected problem in areas like Jamsil-dong, Songpa-gu, in Seoul, this crisis has over time laid bare the depth of administrative incompetence and shoddiness. (당초 송파구 잠실동 등 서울 일부 지역에서 발생한 돌발적인 문제로 치부되었던 이번 사태는 시간이 흐를수록 행정적 무능과 부실의 깊이가 얼마나 깊었는지를 적나라하게 보여주고 있다.)

What is appalling is the pathetic and complacent manner in which the National Election Commission (NEC) explained and handled the situation. The NEC initially attributed the problem to a "voter turnout far exceeding expectations," effectively shifting blame onto the voters. As a professional election management body, preparing for unexpected surges in turnout or emergencies is its most basic duty, yet it offered administrative forecasting failures as an excuse. (경악스러운 건 중앙선관위의 한심하고 안이한 해명과 수습 태도다. 선관위는 초기 “예상치를 크게 웃도는 투표율 증가”를 원인으로 꼽으며 책임을 유권자에게 돌리는 듯한 행태를 보였다. 선거관리 전문 기관으로서 돌발적 투표율 상승이나 비상 상황에 대비하는 건 가장 기본 임무임에도 불구하고, 행정적 예측 실패를 변명으로 내세운 것이다.)

The leadership, including NEC Chairman Noh Tae-ak, instead of immediately expressing remorse and launching a probe right after the incident, showed an attitude of evading responsibility and shifting the problem to lower-tier agencies, stoking public outrage. This incompetence of the NEC and the lax awareness of the government and political circles have led to critical procedural flaws that make the outcomes of elections—the flower of democracy—untrustworthy, escalating into legal and social struggles. (노태악 중앙선거관리위원장을 비롯한 수뇌부는 사태 발생 직후 즉각 책임 통감과 진상 규명에 나서기보다 책임을 회피하고 하급 기관에 문제를 전가하려는 태도를 보여 공분을 키웠다. 이러한 선관위의 무능과 정부·정치권의 안이한 인식은 민주주의의 꽃인 선거 결과를 신뢰할 수 없게 만드는 치명적인 절차적 결함으로 이어졌고, 법적·사회적 투쟁으로 비화하고 있다.)

The most vehemently reacting and taking the lead in this ballot paper catastrophe are undoubtedly the 2030 MZ generation. In a big data related-term analysis conducted by SomeTrend from June 4 to 11, 2026, key words linked to the '2030' generation were overwhelmingly economic in nature, directly tied to survival: stocks, investment, housing prices, real estate, assets, loans, office workers, homes, and "yeonggeul" (stretching finances to the limit). (이번 투표용지 대참사에 대해 가장 격렬하게 반응하며 전면에 나선 주체는 단연 2030 MZ세대다. 썸트랜드(SomeTrend)가 2026년 6월 4~11일 실시한 빅데이터 연관어 분석에서 ’2030′ 세대와 결합한 핵심 단어들은 주식, 투자, 집값, 부동산, 자산, 대출, 직장인, 주택, 영끌 등 철저하게 생존과 직결된 경제적 키워드들이다.)

Correspondingly, emotional words formed a massive cluster: anger, election fraud, young, anxiety, dissatisfaction, criticism, fear, rejection, loss, conflict, and concern. Key words related to 'ballot paper' also included shortage, insufficient, lacking, election fraud, controversy, suspicion, trust, shoddiness, anger, and truth, reflecting the gravity of the situation. (그리고 이에 대응하는 감성어로는 분노, 부정선거, 젊다, 불안, 불만, 비판, 공포, 거부하다, 손해, 갈등, 우려 등이 거대한 군집을 이루고 있다. ‘투표용지’ 관련 핵심 키워드 역시 부족, 부족하다, 모자라다, 부정선거, 논란, 의혹, 신뢰, 부실, 분노, 진상 등으로 나타나 사태의 심각성을 반영한다.)

This fully reflects the harsh reality facing today's 2030 generation. Young people, deprived of opportunities for asset building amid skyrocketing housing prices, cling to stock and virtual asset investments, barely surviving day by day in anxiety and fear while enduring so-called "yeonggeul" and excessive loans. For office workers and job seekers pushed to the brink of economic survival, the only equal right granted to them was the "right to vote." Elections were the only procedural avenue of justice through which young people, without money or connections, could make their voices heard on an equal footing with older generations. (이는 현재의 2030 세대가 처한 가혹한 현실을 고스란히 반영한다. 폭등한 집값 속에서 자산 형성 기회를 박탈당한 청년들은 주식과 가상자산 투자에 매달리고, 이른바 ‘영끌’과 과도한 대출을 감내하며 하루하루를 불안과 공포 속에서 버텨내고 있는 실정이다. 경제적 생존의 한계선에 내몰린 직장인과 취업 준비생들에게 유일하게 평등하게 주어졌던 권리가 바로 ‘투표권’이었다. 돈도 배경도 없는 청년들이 기성 세대와 대등하게 사회적 목소리를 낼 수 있는 유일한 절차적 정의의 통로가 바로 선거였던 것이다.)

However, when even the most basic state-managed system—elections—failed to properly supply ballot papers, turning into a lawless mess, the 2030 generation experienced a psychological shock and began to express rejection of the entire system. From the MZ generation's perspective, which values fairness and procedural legitimacy above all else, the NEC's ballot paper shortage and makeshift measures like photocopying represented a collapse of social rules. (그러나 국가가 관리하는 가장 기초적 시스템인 선거마저 투표용지조차 제대로 공급하지 못하는 무법천지가 되자, 2030 세대는 정신적 충격과 함께 시스템 전체에 대한 거부감을 드러내기 시작했다. 공정성과 절차적 정당성을 그 어떤 가치보다 무겁게 받아들이는 MZ세대 관점에서, 선관위 투표용지 부족과 사본 복사 같은 주먹구구식 조치는 사회적 룰의 붕괴를 의미했다.)

A collective awakening emerged: "I'm already aggrieved by the economic losses and asset inequality I face, and now the state is trying to steal my sacred vote and deceive me?" Ultimately, the massive texts pointing to 'election fraud' and 'anger' in big data amount to an ultimatum from young people, who have lost faith in the system's fairness, directed at the state and older generations. (“내가 처한 경제적 손해와 자산 불평등도 억울한데, 나라가 내 신성한 한 표마저 빼앗아 가고 속이려 드는가”라는 집단적 각성이 일어난 것이다. 결국 빅데이터가 가리키는 ‘부정선거’와 ‘분노’의 거대한 텍스트는 시스템의 공정성을 불신하게 된 청년들이 국가와 기성세대를 향해 던지는 최후통첩과 다름없다.)

This anger has not stayed online but has moved into offline action. In a political climate where a joint police-prosecution investigation team has conducted large-scale raids on the central NEC, the Seoul Metropolitan NEC, and key district NECs in Gangnam, Seocho, Songpa, Dongjak, and Gwangjin where the incident occurred, the 2030 generation is organizing nationwide protests and rallies, pouring into the streets. The most notable feature of this resistance movement is that ideological and gender divisions within the younger generation have completely disappeared, uniting men and women under the single banner of 'defending the right to vote,' sharing intense anger on equal terms. (분노는 온라인상에 머물지 않고 오프라인 행동으로 옮겨붙었다. 중앙선관위와 서울시 선관위를 비롯해 사태가 발생한 강남, 서초, 송파, 동작, 광진 등 주요 구 선관위에 대한 검경 합동수사본부의 대대적인 압수수색이 자행되는 정국 속에서, 2030 세대는 전국적인 반발 집회와 시위를 조직하며 광장으로 쏟아져 나오고 있다. 이번 저항 운동의 가장 주목할 만한 특징은 청년 세대 내부의 이념적, 젠더적 분열이 완전히 사라지고 ‘참정권 수호’라는 단일 기치하에 남녀가 전혀 다르지 않게 격렬한 분노를 공유하며 단일 대오를 형성했다는 점이다.)

The gender conflicts and conservative-progressive divides that have split youth politics in South Korea for years have been neutralized in the face of this ballot paper catastrophe. At university campuses and urban protest sites, young men and women stand shoulder to shoulder, chanting slogans like "Dissolve the NEC that mocks democracy!" and "Restore the stolen right to vote through a full re-election!" (지난 수년간 한국 사회 청년 정치를 갈라놓았던 젠더 갈등이나 진보·보수의 진영 논리는 이번 투표용지 대참사 앞에서 무력화됐다. 대학가와 도심 집회 현장에는 남녀 청년들이 어깨를 나란히 하고 “민주주의 기만하는 선관위는 해체하라”, “빼앗긴 참정권, 전면 재선거로 회복하라”는 구호를 외치고 있다.)

They do not see this crisis as a tool for political strife over gender issues or advantages for specific parties. Instead, they approach it as a fundamental issue of justice, where the state has ignored young voters and infringed on their basic rights. The shared sorrow and anger felt equally by young women and young men have solidified their solidarity, serving as a core engine that has spread the protest momentum nationwide. (이들은 이번 사태를 남녀 문제나 특정 정당 유리함을 따지는 정쟁의 도구로 보지 않는다. 국가가 청년 유권자를 무시하고 기본권을 침해한 본질적인 정의의 문제로 접근하고 있는 것이다. 청년 여성과 청년 남성이 동일하게 느끼는 서글픔과 분노는 이들의 연대를 더욱 공고하게 만들었으며, 시위의 동력을 전국적으로 확산시키는 핵심 엔진이 됐다.)

At the same time, university campuses have broken their silence and risen up. Major universities including Seoul National University, Yonsei University, and Korea University, as well as numerous student councils in the Seoul metropolitan area and provinces, have issued back-to-back "state affairs declarations," raising the alarm. These declarations differ from past politically motivated ones. Each declaration thunderously asserts, "Incompetent established political powers and administrative officials who cannot even manage the physical foundation of democracy—ballot papers—must kneel and apologize before the younger generation." (동시에 대학가 역시 침묵을 깨고 일어섰다. 서울대를 비롯한 연세대, 고려대 등 주요 대학은 물론 수도권과 지방 수많은 대학 총학생회들이 잇따라 ‘시국선언문’을 발표하며 사태의 심각성을 끌어올리고 있다. 각 대학 총학생회 시국선언문은 과거 정치적 목적을 띤 시국선언과 궤를 달리한다. 선언문들은 하나같이 “민주주의의 물리적 기초인 투표용지조차 관리하지 못하는 무능한 기성 정치 권력과 행정 관료들은 청년 세대 앞에 무릎 꿇고 사죄하라”고 일갈하고 있다.)

The student councils present specific demands: a thorough investigation through parliamentary audits and special counsel, comprehensive structural reform of the NEC, and the establishment of an independent reform oversight body with citizen participation. They solemnly declare that if these demands are not met, they will move toward full-scale resistance struggle. This organized and intense state affairs declaration by university campuses is a signal that the crisis level perceived by young people has gone beyond mere election mismanagement to a point of state system bankruptcy. The deepest essence of this crisis, as noted by political and academic experts, is that the administrative disaster of the ballot paper shortage acted as a decisive 'trigger effect,' detonating the anger long accumulated in the younger generation's hearts toward the entrenched older generation. The arrows of anger felt by the 2030 generation target not just NEC officials, but the older generation that has dominated South Korea's political, economic, and social hegemony and oppressed young people's right to survival—especially the 'activist (386/586) generation' that has firmly entrenched itself as the privileged class, having monopolized democratization as its own asset. (정치권과 사회학계 전문가들이 주목하는 이번 사태 가장 깊은 본질은, 투표용지 부족이라는 행정적 참사가 청년 세대 마음 깊은 곳에 응축되어 있던 기득권 기성세대에 대한 분노를 한꺼번에 폭발시키는 결정적 ‘방아쇠 효과(Trigger Effect)’로 작동했다는 점이다. 2030 세대가 체감하는 분노의 화살은 단순히 선관위 관료들을 넘어, 대한민국의 정치·경제·사회의 헤게모니를 장악하고 청년들의 생존권을 압박해 온 기성세대, 특히 과거 민주화를 독점적 자산으로 삼아 기득권층으로 공고히 자리 잡은 ‘운동권(386·586) 세대’를 정조준하고 있다.)

The current privileged class in South Korea, centered on former activists, has always justified its power by lecturing the younger generation on 'democracy and morality.' But what is the true face of the system they have built and managed? They have handed young people a 'real estate surge' and a 'housing price hell,' making it impossible for them to own a home in Seoul even after a lifetime of work, and they have severed the social ladder, fundamentally blocking opportunities for 'asset building.' While young people, scrambling for loans to survive, shed tears of blood in the stock and investment markets, the privileged class has solidified its asset cartel and passed down wealth across generations. Despite harsh economic inequality, young people have lived faithfully, trusting the system's rules. A fundamental question of legitimacy has been raised: "Those who tried to teach us about democracy and justice—can't they even guarantee the most basic right to vote due to their own incompetence and shoddiness?" The incompetence, complacency, and flimsy attempts to evade responsibility by the older generation have triggered in young people, beyond simple political disappointment, a 'survival-level sense of crisis' that they cannot entrust their future to this incompetent generation. (“우리에게 민주주의와 정의를 가르치려 들던 자들이, 자신들의 무능과 부실로 가장 기본적인 투표권조차 보장하지 못하는가”라는 근본적인 정당성 의문이 제기된 것이다. 기성세대의 무능과 안이함, 그리고 사태를 모면하려는 얄팍한 대응은 청년들에게 단순한 정치적 실망을 넘어, 자신들의 미래를 이 무능한 세대에게 맡겨둘 수 없다는 ‘생존권 차원의 위기의식’을 촉발시켰다.)

Ultimately, the fierce resistance of the 2030 generation, ignited by the ballot paper catastrophe, is a collective movement to reestablish sovereignty, aimed at judging the hypocrisy and incompetence of the privileged activist generation. Young people no longer want a technical fix like replenishing ballot papers. They are declaring a historic turning point: to dismantle the older generation's cartel that has infringed on their right to vote and threatened their right to survival, and to reestablish the broken rules of justice and fairness with their own hands. If the political world and older generation fail to grasp the essence of this anger and continue with complacent excuses and stalling, the flames of this struggle to defend democracy and survival, ignited by the 2030 generation, could escalate into a massive explosion that consumes the entire established system.
